pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.28 a.1
pairs.question: Utrum in Deo sint aliquae relationes reales?
pairs.answer: Relationes quaedam sunt in divinis realiter.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article header (line 30), a genuine indirect interrogative (utrum...). Answer is the operative first sentence of the Respondeo (line 44), with the framing tag 'Respondeo dicendum quod' dropped and the first word capitalized. The window ends at the first full stop; what follows ('Ad cuius evidentiam, considerandum est...') is the supporting elaboration, not the answer itself.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.28 a.2
pairs.question: Utrum relatio in Deo sit idem quod sua essentia?
pairs.answer: Patet ergo quod in Deo non est aliud esse relationis et esse essentiae, sed unum et idem.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article header (line 57). The Respondeo opens with a non-answering preamble about Gilbert Porretanus's error and a long demonstration ('Respondeo dicendum quod circa hoc dicitur Gilbertus Porretanus errasse...'), which does not answer the question, so per the skip-non-answering-preamble guidance the answer start is advanced to the operative concluding sentence at the end of line 72. That sentence directly affirms the identity of relation and essence in God; it is a single contiguous full sentence quoted verbatim.

pairs.locus: Aquinas, Summa Theologiae I q.28 a.3
pairs.question: Utrum relationes quae sunt in Deo, realiter ab invicem distinguantur?
pairs.answer: Unde oportet quod in Deo sit realis distinctio, non quidem secundum rem absolutam, quae est essentia, in qua est summa unitas et simplicitas; sed secundum rem relativam.
pairs.derivation: Question is the article header (line 82). The Respondeo opens with a premise-building preamble ('ex eo quod aliquid alicui attribuitur... oportet quod realiter sit ibi oppositio. Relativa autem oppositio in sui ratione includit distinctionem.') that argues toward but does not yet state the answer, so the start is advanced to the concluding sentence ('Unde oportet quod in Deo sit realis distinctio...', line 94), which directly affirms a real distinction. Quoted verbatim and contiguous to its full stop; nothing follows in the Respondeo.
